

`internal/review/anchor.go`, no I/O, the four stages of WL-REQ-1773 as
Decisions spell them:

```go
// Relocate finds where the quote anchored at old[start:end] now sits in new,
// climbing crit's four-stage ladder (WL-REQ-1773). ok=false means drifted:
// the caller marks the thread obsolete (WL-REQ-1317). Offsets are UTF-8
// bytes; a returned range always lies on character boundaries.
func Relocate(old, new string, start, end int, quote string) (newStart, newEnd int, stage string, ok bool)
```

First test:

```go
func TestRelocate(t *testing.T) {
    old := "a\nb\ntarget := 1\nc\n"
    q := "target := 1"
    s, e := strings.Index(old, q), strings.Index(old, q)+len(q)
    cases := []struct {
        name      string
        newText   string
        wantQuote bool
        wantStage string
    }{
        {"unchanged", old, true, "exact"},
        {"two lines inserted above", "x\ny\n" + old, true, "lcs"},
        {"line reindented", "a\nb\n    target := 1\nc\n", true, "fuzzy"},
        {"moved far away", "a\nb\nc\n" + strings.Repeat("z\n", 40) + "target := 1\n", true, "scan"},
        {"deleted", "a\nb\nc\n", false, "drifted"},
        {"multibyte text before the quote", "æøå\n" + old, true, "lcs"},
    }
    // for each: ns, ne, stage, ok := Relocate(old, c.newText, s, e, q);
    // ok == c.wantQuote; stage == c.wantStage; ok implies newText[ns:ne] == q.
}
```

Also test that a quote shorter than 8 bytes never fuzzy-matches, and that
with two `scan` hits the one nearest the predicted offset wins.

Matching is whitespace-insensitive at every stage (Decisions): a run of
whitespace in the quote matches any run of whitespace in the candidate, and
the returned range covers the candidate's own bytes. Add the case "quote
across a rewrapped line survives": old `"one two\nthree four\n"`, quote `"two\nthree"`,
new `"one two three four\n"` → ok, `new[ns:ne] == "two three"`, stage
`exact`. This is what the first normalising write of an old body
(WL-REQ-1867) does to every wrapped paragraph.
